subject: Prospect Q&A: Regional processing locations, subprocessors, and deletion handoff
messages:
From: Sam Park <sam.park@mednexa.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@mednexa.com>
Date: 2026-11-09T09:12:00Z
Subject: Initial: Where does data get processed?

Hi Tessa,

Thanks for walking us through Redwood last week. As part of our procurement checklist we need a concise answer to where customer data is actually processed when we call the hosted API:

- Which physical regions do inference requests touch when we select EU region?
- Do any subprocessors or transit hops sit in the US/other territories?
- How long is request data retained in any cache or logs, and how is deletion handled at the service edge?

Can you share a short written summary and any supporting evidence (subprocessor list, diagram)? We need this for our security team and GRC review.

Appreciate it — Sam
Security & Compliance, MedNexa
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
To: Sam Park <sam.park@mednexa.com>
Cc: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@mednexa.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-09T12:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Initial: Where does data get processed?

Hi Sam — thanks for the clear list of asks. High-level summary below; attaching a concise subprocessor inventory and an execution map.

Short answers (EU-region requests):

1) Regional execution: When you select the EU region in the Redwood Console/ API, inference is routed to GPU capacity located in our EU cloud regions (Frankfurt and Dublin). For hosted customers pinned to EU, the active compute for token generation executes within those regions by default.

2) Transit & subprocessors: Data may traverse additional internal control-plane services (control plane in our US tenancy for account management) for orchestration, but model execution and ephemeral KV/prefix caches stay in EU execution nodes. Subprocessors that may process telemetry/metrics or billing are listed in the attached mednexa_subproc_list.xlsx — a subset of those operate in the US for billing/analytics; we flag data that is PII and do not include user request text in billing exports.

3) Caching and logs retention:
- Ephemeral in-memory KV/prefix caches: exist on execution nodes and are not persisted to disk; typical TTLs are short (seconds to minutes) depending on your configured batching/caching rules.
- Request logs (traces/observability): by default retained for 30 days; can be configured to 7/30/90 days per plan.
- Persistent artifacts (audit logs, billing records): retained per contract; we can redact request bodies from billing records on request.

4) Deletion & erasure:
- Runtime caches are evicted automatically and not archived.
- For hosted customers, we provide an API to request account-level erasure of request bodies and associated traces; we will provide a deletion ticket and ETA (standard SLA 7 business days for hosted API).
- For Private (VPC/on-prem) deployments, control over deletion is customer-managed; Redwood will provide playbooks and APIs to coordinate erasure.

Attachments: mednexa_subproc_list.xlsx (current as of today), redwood_execution_map.png (visual of control plane vs execution plane), SOC2-summary.pdf (high-level attestation).

If useful, we can produce an export that strips any billing/analytics fields containing request text and provide a signed attestation for the records.

Would you like a short (15 min) follow-up call with our infra/security PM to walk the execution map?

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference
From: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@mednexa.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: Sam Park <sam.park@mednexa.com>
Date: 2026-11-10T08:20:00Z
Subject: Re: Initial: Where does data get processed?

Thanks Tessa — this is helpful. A couple quick clarifications from our security team:

- You say control-plane orchestration is in the US. Does that ever include request payloads (full prompts) or only metadata (timestamps, request IDs)?
- For the ephemeral caches on execution nodes: are there any autosave or crash-dump behaviors that might write KV cache or request snippets to disk?
- If EU capacity is exhausted and Redwood falls back to another region, what is the policy/notice to customers? Will requests fail closed or be routed to non-EU nodes?

Also can you point us to the SOC2 artifact or the certificate cover page (not the full report)? We can accept an executive summary for procurement.

Appreciate the fast response — Jordan
Head of IT Risk, MedNexa
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Cc: Sam Park <sam.park@mednexa.com>, Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@mednexa.com>
Date: 2026-11-10T10:10:00Z
Subject: Re: Initial: Where does data get processed?

Internal note + reply to Jordan and Sam (putting answers inline):

Jordan — quick inline:
- Control plane: only metadata, account identifiers, job scheduling info. We do NOT route full request bodies through the US control plane for EU-pinned customers. We redact request bodies from control-plane telemetry by default; see attached SOC2-summary.pdf that documents our evidence folder.
- Crash-dumps: execution nodes run with mlock and we configure the process such that caches are in-memory and not written to swap; we do collect core dumps only with explicit engineering-level opt-in and they are scrubbed of user content. 
- Fallback policy: default policy is fail-closed for EU-pinned strict residency customers. We will not route EU-pinned requests to non-EU nodes without explicit customer opt-in. For non-pinned customers we have region preference and automated fallback to nearest available pool; customers are notified via the Console and via webhooks when fallback occurs.

Action items (Redwood):
- Marissa to generate one-page evidence: subprocessor locations + redaction controls (ETA 2 business days) [ACTION: marissa.cole@redwood.com]
- Connor to prepare a short note on crash-dump/operational protections and confirm swap/no-swap configuration (ETA 1 business day) [ACTION: connor.obrien@redwood.com]
- Tessa to schedule a 15 min walkthrough with MedNexa security if they want it (pending)

We will send the two supporting artifacts as a link and attach the summary to this thread.

-Marissa
Director, Applied ML Ops — Redwood Inference
